files.purpose: The hand-written release history of Droppy Code in Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 form, newest first, covering 1.0.0 (2026-09-13) through 1.6.2 (2026-09-18) plus an undated `## [Unreleased]` block at the top. Line 5 makes it the machine-read source for two release scripts: scripts/publish_release.sh takes the section whose heading matches the version in project.yml, passes it through `python3 scripts/build_changelog.py --section "$VERSION"` (publish_release.sh:21), which promotes every `### ` heading to `## ` (build_changelog.py:126-127 `out.append("## " + line[4:])`), and publishes the result as the GitLab release notes that Settings › About parses into its New features / Bug fixes / Refinements cards, and scripts/build_changelog.py turns every versioned section into website/changelog.json. At B2 it is the only place in the repository that describes, in prose, what 1.6.1 and 1.6.2 changed for the user (concise replies, thread forwarding, custom MCP servers, the inline About release-note cards, renamed Codex and CommandCode plans, the favicon lookup order, persisted Hydra auto-hide) and what has merged but not shipped (Hydra token and timing breakdown, restored design, concurrent native read tools, the token-activity measured/inherited split).
key_symbols: line 3: format statement: follows Keep a Changelog https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/; 'versions are the release tags without the `v`'
line 5: release-tooling contract paragraph (publish_release.sh, build_changelog.py, `## [Unreleased]` skipped by both scripts, `### Thanks` form, `python3 scripts/release_credits.py`)

line 7: '## [Unreleased]' (### New features line 9, ### Refinements line 12, ### Bug fixes line 17). This is the only section in the file with Refinements before Bug fixes; every versioned section runs New features, Bug fixes, Refinements (e.g. 1.6.1 at 34/37/43, 1.3.0 at 244/260/280).

line 47: '## [1.6.0] - 2026-09-18' (summary 49, ### New features 51, ### Bug fixes 57, ### Refinements 62, ### Thanks 67)

subsection headings used: '### New features', '### Bug fixes', '### Refinements', '### Thanks' (a `### Thanks` block only under 1.6.2 and 1.6.0). 1.5.0 also credits a contributor, but inline: line 186 ends 'Contributed by nik1tsyganov.' inside a New features bullet, so build_changelog.py puts it in sections[].items and website/changelog.json's 1.5.0 entry has "thanks": [] (json line 302, item at json line 283).
calls_into: scripts/publish_release.sh: reads MARKETING_VERSION from project.yml (line 17 `sed -nE 's/^[[:space:]]*MARKETING_VERSION:[[:space:]]*"([^"]+)".*/\1/p' project.yml | head -1`), runs `python3 scripts/build_changelog.py --section "$VERSION" > "$NOTES"` (line 21; failure prints 'No ## [$VERSION] section in CHANGELOG.md. Add one before publishing.'), and refuses to publish unless `grep -qE '^## (New features|Bug fixes|Refinements)' "$NOTES"` matches (line 30-33, message 'needs at least one of the three headings: ## New features, ## Bug fixes, ## Refinements.'). It then runs `python3 scripts/release_credits.py --check "$NOTES"` (line 36). No summary paragraph is required.

scripts/build_changelog.py: parses this file into website/changelog.json; its RELEASE_RE (line 20 of that script) is `^## \[(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\](?: - (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}))?\s*$`, so `## [Unreleased]` never matches and is skipped; its strip_emphasis (lines 54-55) deletes every `**`, `__`, `*` and `_` from each bullet (cross-reference read by grep/sed only, file not in this bundle)

scripts/build_changelog.py extract_section (lines 114-131, the --section mode used for the GitLab notes): trims leading/trailing blank lines, rewrites each line starting `### ` to `## ` + the rest, and passes every other line (the summary paragraph, bullets, the Thanks bullets) through unchanged. Unlike parse_notes it does NOT call strip_emphasis and does NOT reorder sections, so the GitLab release text keeps the file's section order and its underscores and asterisks.

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/AboutUpdateViews.swift UpdateReleaseNotesDigest.parseNotes (lines 100-130): reads the GitLab notes; category(forHeader:) (153-166) strips any number of leading `#`, so it would accept `###` as well as `##`, and maps 'new features'/'new', 'bug fixes'/'fixes'/'bugs', 'refinements'/'improvements'; any other heading such as `## Thanks` sets current = nil (114-118) so its bullets are left out (doc comment 64-66); plain lines such as a summary paragraph are ignored. Sections are emitted in ReleaseNoteCategory.allCases order (line 120; enum order newFeatures, bugFixes, refinements at 12-15) and the cards are laid out with ForEach(ReleaseNoteCategory.allCases) (198), so the About cards never follow file order. strippedInlineMarkdown (180-185) removes only links, `**bold**` and backticks, so underscores survive in-app (e.g. 'self_serve_business_prolite') while backticks are removed; the website keeps backticks but loses underscores.
scripts/release_credits.py: prints the `### Thanks` block for the changes since the previous tag (line 5)
project.yml: holds the version (MARKETING_VERSION "1.6.2") that publish_release.sh matches against a heading
state_owned: No runtime state. Owns the canonical wording of every release note that reaches the GitLab release (and therefore the in-app About cards) and the website.
side_effects: None by itself. Per line 5, publishing stops until every outside contributor is named in the version's `### Thanks` block, and the next release renames `## [Unreleased]` to its version and date. When the Unreleased block ships with its current order (Refinements line 12 before Bug fixes line 17), the raw GitLab release description keeps that file order (extract_section does not reorder), while the website (SECTION_ORDER = ["New features", "Bug fixes", "Refinements"], build_changelog.py:29) and the in-app About cards (ReleaseNoteCategory.allCases) both show New features, Bug fixes, Refinements.
platform_assumptions: Every versioned summary paragraph from 1.0.0 to 1.6.0 ends 'Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later. Signed and notarized.'; 1.6.1 and 1.6.2 carry no summary paragraph at all.
1.6.2: custom MCP server 'secret fields stored in the Keychain' (a Windows port must map to its own secret store, e.g. Credential Manager / DPAPI).

1.6.1: a macOS 27 AppKit/SwiftUI failure mode: 'a popover's window coming on screen can make the framework's remote view throw from inside the notification that announces it', AppKit catches the exception during a SwiftUI layout pass and stops the app; the fix wraps the app's notification posts to catch the raise, log it 'with the raising observer's frames', and carry on. NotificationCenter/NSException semantics have no Windows equivalent.
1.6.1: favicon lookup uses DuckDuckGo's icon service first and Google's service as fallback, and removes solid white backgrounds (network services and image processing to replicate).
1.6.0: project marks may be an emoji or an SF Symbol (SF Symbols are Apple-only; Windows needs a substitute glyph set).

Older entries name macOS-only mechanisms: Keychain for API keys (1.2.0, 1.1.0), Liquid Glass knob and glass themes (1.2.0, 1.1.0), 'traffic lights' (only 1.2.0, lines 322 and 331; 1.1.1 line 344 says 'the window buttons sat too high beside the chat's chrome; they drop to its centre line as they move over' without the phrase), window drag region and title-bar layout crashes (1.5.0, 1.4.1, 1.5.4), key view loop owned by AppKit (1.3.0), VoiceOver label 'No cap' (1.5.6), disk image drag-to-Applications window (1.5.5), ⌘ shortcuts (1.5.3), iMessage's bubble (1.1.0), native text selection runs (1.5.3).
persisted_fields: No app persistence. Document format fields: version heading `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD`; optional prose summary paragraph under the heading; bullets `- ` under `### New features`, `### Bug fixes`, `### Refinements`; Thanks bullets in the form `- Name (@gitlab-handle): what they did (!MR).`.

Behavioural persistence facts stated in the notes: 1.6.2 'The Hydra sidebar auto-hide setting persists and defaults to off.'; 1.6.2 custom MCP secret fields stored in the Keychain; 1.6.1 concise replies option in Settings, General takes effect on the next message; 1.6.0 'a new install starts on the compact one' (activity list); 1.5.5 Chronological order and Heads at once 'Off by default'; 1.3.0 'The last Hydra pair is remembered and applied to new chats.'
ui_elements: Settings › About cards 'New features', 'Bug fixes', 'Refinements' (1.6.1): each opens its section 'in a card under the row instead of in a popover', notes 'scroll with' the page, and 'tapping the card again, or the card's close button, folds them away'.
Settings, General: Concise AI replies option (1.6.1), keeps 'replies, code comments and Hydra head work focused', effective on the next message.
Thread forwarding (1.6.1): 'A thread can also be forwarded to a new thread, carrying its request and context so the work can continue with another model.'

Codex usage panel plan names (1.6.1): `pro` -> 'Pro 20x' (was 'Pro'; the $200 Pro tier), `prolite` -> 'Pro 5x' (was 'Prolite'), self-serve business Pro Lite -> 'Business Premium' (was 'self_serve_business_prolite').

CommandCode plan names (1.6.1, line 41): 'CommandCode plan names now match commandcode.ai's tiers, including Go, GOAT, Pro, Provider, Max 10×, Max 20× and Teams Pro' (the list is explicitly partial: 'including'; U+00D7 multiplication sign, unlike Codex's ASCII 'x'); 'an unfamiliar plan ID is still shown in readable words instead of disappearing' ('still': the readable-words fallback already existed and is not new in 1.6.1).
Custom MCP servers in Settings (1.6.2): added via 'a local command or a remote HTTP address'.
Hydra panel (Unreleased): 'recorded lead and head tokens by provider and model, with queue, startup, execution and landing timings where available'.
Token activity grid (Unreleased): 'the line under the grid names how much of the year's total those are' (inherited totals).

Older strings kept for reference: "Worked for …" fold line (1.6.0), 'Cancel' and 'New thread' usage-limit buttons (1.6.0), 'Auto-hide heads in the sidebar' (1.6.0, Settings, Hydra, Heads), 'Heads at once' Off/1-8 with infinity sign read as 'No cap' (1.5.5/1.5.6), 'One panel' / 'A panel each' (1.5.3), 'The chat's last pair' (1.5.0), 'Banked resets · 2 available' (1.4.1), 'Update & restart' (1.1.0), 'Show activity while working' (1.3.0).
feature_notes: Unreleased New features (line 10): Hydra's panel shows recorded lead and head tokens by provider and model, with queue, startup, execution and landing timings where available.

Unreleased Refinements (lines 13-15): 'Restored the previous Droppy Code design and removed the judgment service integration.'; Hydra 'parses streamed delegations incrementally, reuses incremental checkout snapshots and avoids repeated timeline scans while waiting to land edits'; 'Native API providers run up to four independent automatic read tools concurrently and load bounded root project guidelines.'

Unreleased Bug fixes (line 18): token activity separates measured from inherited: daily totals recorded before spend kept its source are still counted, and the line under the grid states their share of the year's total instead of presenting them as measured.
Per line 5, Unreleased is 'Work that has merged but not shipped', so these four areas are described as already merged at the B2 commit even though the build is labelled 1.6.2 build 20.

1.6.2 (lines 20-30): one New feature (custom MCP servers: local command or remote HTTP address, secret fields in the Keychain), one Bug fix (Hydra sidebar auto-hide persists, defaults to off), Thanks: 'Nikita Tsyganov (@nik1tsyganov): the Hydra auto-hide setting (!358).' and 'Bryan Galdámez (@JosueGalRe): custom MCP server definitions and settings (!305).' No summary paragraph.

1.6.1 (lines 32-45): New features: Concise AI replies option in Settings, General plus thread forwarding. Bug fixes (4): notification-post raise guard (macOS 27 popover, reports of September 18 from the About release-note cards); About cards expand inline; Codex plan names; CommandCode plan names. Refinements (2): favicon lookup DuckDuckGo first, Google fallback, solid white backgrounds removed; moving a thread to another project uses 'the same project-move path everywhere' and 'automatically expands and reveals the moved thread in the sidebar'. No summary paragraph and no Thanks.

1.6.0 summary (line 49) and items unchanged from B1: Netlify MCP catalog entry, project marks (emoji or SF Symbol), usage-limit Cancel / New thread notice, Auto-hide heads in the sidebar off by default, GitLab 19.4 404 handling with proxy 502, scroll and diff performance fixes, folded finished turns, Chronological order switch removed; Thanks for René (@diazdesandi) (!307, !308), Bryan Galdámez (@JosueGalRe) (!283, !285, !304, !306), Nikita Tsyganov (@nik1tsyganov) (!293).

Formatting quirks: lines 124-125, 152-153, 161-162, 179-180, 196-197, 217-218, 228-229, 238-239, 299-300, 332-333, 348-349 and 383-384 are double blank lines before the next heading; the file has no trailing blank line (last line 400 is the 1.0.0 'A terminal under every thread.' bullet). Working-tree bytes are CRLF (git index is LF, core.autocrlf=true); the sha256 above is of the CRLF working-tree bytes, 42292 bytes.

Bullets containing underscores or asterisks lose them when build_changelog.py writes the website JSON (e.g. line 40 `self_serve_business_prolite` and line 68 `search_text`), so this file, not the JSON, is the verbatim source.

B1->B2: 33 lines added, none removed (367 -> 400 lines). A new `## [Unreleased]` block (New features 1 item, Refinements 3, Bug fixes 1) was inserted at lines 9-18; new headings `## [1.6.2] - 2026-09-18` (lines 20-30, including its two-entry Thanks block) and `## [1.6.1] - 2026-09-18` (line 32) plus 1.6.1's `### New features` item (lines 34-35) were inserted. The three bug fixes that sat under B1's `## [Unreleased]` (notification raise guard, inline About cards, Codex plan names) are now the first three items of 1.6.1's Bug fixes (lines 38-40, text unchanged), followed by a new CommandCode plan-name item (line 41) and a new `### Refinements` with the favicon and thread-move items (lines 43-45). Everything from `## [1.6.0]` down is byte-identical in content.

Licence history: 1.3.0 Refinements (line 293) already says 'The license is GNU AGPL v3 with attribution.', yet B1's project.yml line 46 still set INFOPLIST_KEY_NSHumanReadableCopyright: "Droppy Code, the coding app by Droppy. MIT License."; so the MIT string in the macOS About panel contradicted the changelog from 1.3.0 until B2 replaced it with the AGPL copyright line. The port's About surface must show the B2 AGPL string.
unresolved_questions: Resolved: 1.6.1 and 1.6.2 having no summary paragraph is fine for every consumer. publish_release.sh:30 requires only one `^## (New features|Bug fixes|Refinements)` heading, extract_section passes any summary through unchanged, the About parser ignores plain lines, and website/assets/js/changelog.js:302-303 (`var summary = typeof release.summary === "string" ? release.summary.trim() : ""; if (summary) {`) simply renders no summary paragraph for "".

'Restored the previous Droppy Code design and removed the judgment service integration' names neither the design being restored nor what the 'judgment service' was; the Swift sources and the B1->B2 source diff must define it.

'load bounded root project guidelines' gives no bound (bytes, lines or file names) and 'up to four independent automatic read tools' does not name which tools count as automatic reads; both must come from the native provider source.
The build number 1.6.1 shipped with is not recorded here (B1 1.6.0 was build 19, B2 1.6.2 is build 20).

INFOPLIST_KEY_CFBundleDisplayName = "Droppy Code" (Release, 293) / "Droppy Code Dev" (Debug, 317) is also a persistence key: Text.swift:4 `static let name = Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleDisplayName") as? String ?? "Droppy Code"`. APIKeychain.swift:31,45,61 and MCPKeychain.swift:15,39,55 use `kSecAttrService as String: AppInfo.name` (accounts: the provider account, e.g. 'Command Code API Key', or 'MCP <server> <field>'), and Storage.swift:21-22 puts library.json, threads, attachments and wallpaper under Application Support/<AppInfo.name>; MCPBridgeSource.swift:243 and CommandCodeAPI.swift:443 use '<AppInfo.name>/MCP' and '<AppInfo.name>/CommandCode' there. So Release keeps secrets under Keychain service "Droppy Code" and Debug under "Droppy Code Dev"; renaming the display name orphans stored API keys, MCP secrets and the library folder. The Windows secret store and data folder must reproduce these names.

files.purpose: The XcodeGen spec from which DroppyCode.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj is generated, and the file whose MARKETING_VERSION the release script matches against a CHANGELOG heading. It declares the project name DroppyCode, the SwiftTerm 1.20.0 package, the base build settings (version 1.6.2, build 20, arm64 only, Swift 6.0, macOS 26.0), and the single macOS application target with its synced source folder, the three legal resource files, bundle identity, Info.plist keys and the Debug/Release overrides.

calls_into: MARKETING_VERSION (line 13) is read by three scripts, all requiring the double-quoted form: scripts/publish_release.sh:17 and scripts/release.sh:19 `sed -nE 's/^[[:space:]]*MARKETING_VERSION:[[:space:]]*"([^"]+)".*/\1/p' project.yml | head -1`, and scripts/release_credits.py:25 `VERSION_RE = re.compile(r'^\s*MARKETING_VERSION:\s*"([^"]+)"\s*$', re.MULTILINE)` (read at line 37, searched at line 40). An unquoted `MARKETING_VERSION: 1.6.2` yields an empty VERSION in both shell scripts (publish_release.sh would then fail at `build_changelog.py --section ""`) and None in release_credits.py.
state_owned: The authored version pair MARKETING_VERSION "1.6.2" / CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION "20" and all authored build settings listed above. The double quotes on lines 13-14 are load-bearing for MARKETING_VERSION: the release scripts' regexes only match a quoted value (see calls_into).
side_effects: Running XcodeGen regenerates project.pbxproj from this spec.
Resource entries copy the three legal files into the app bundle; the package entry makes Xcode fetch SwiftTerm.
platform_assumptions: platform: macOS, deployment target 26.0, arm64 only, Swift 6.0, XcodeGen syncedFolder (Xcode 16+ project format).
Developer ID Application signing with Hardened Runtime (notarized direct distribution).
Objective-C bridging header in DroppyCode/App/Window (AppKit interop).
SwiftTerm as the terminal emulator; asset-catalog AppIcon; Info.plist keys synthesized by Xcode.
